title: role-onboarding-signal-radar-and-communal-handbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical handbook for the first-touch onboarding experience that centers on observable signals (the "signal radar") rather than long static checklists. Goal: reduce early friction, speed time-to-impact, and surface retention risks within 30 days.

Audience:
- Hiring managers, hiring panel leads, people ops partners, onboarding mentors.
- Works for IC hires (engineers, infra, product) and small manager hires with small edits.

Principles (quick):
- Prioritize actions that create measurable outputs in week 1 (PR, doc, demo).
- Pair social onboarding + technical tasks — social anchors help retention.
- Surface risk early and plan mitigations (2-week check-ins, mentor swap).
- Keep artifacts communal (templates in /onboard-templates) so new hires can self-serve.

PREBOARDING (7–14 days before start) — minimal required items:
- Account access checklist (okta, email, slack, vpn, corp VPN, git access): assigned to eng manager.
- Hardware dispatch confirmed (laptop shipped, power adapter, VPN token).
- Role one-pager (manager): 3 outcomes for first 30 days + 3 quick wins. Share with hire and mentor.
- Slack intro message draft (manager + peer buddy): include calendar invites for day1 lunch.
- Learning path pointer: 2 onboarding readme docs + 1 small code walkthrough PR to comment on.
- Calendar blocks: Day1 90m welcome, Day2 60m tech walkthrough, Day7 30m 1:1 ops check.
- Note to people ops: create payroll/benefits welcome + timezone-aware all-hands invite.

DAY 0–7: Activation micro-sprint (outputs > signals)
- Week goal: submit one small PR / write one short explainer doc / demo a config.
- Day0: Slack intro + engineering triage channel added.
- Day1: 90m onboarding session: orientation(20m), team charters(20m), infra intro(25m), calendar sync(25m).
- Pairing: schedule 2 x 60m pairing sessions within first 5 days with assigned mentor and fellow new hire (if available).
- Quick-win checklist (manager):
  * Repo cloned & tests run locally
  * Credentials to sandbox verified
  * First-line doc created in /docs/new-hires/<name> with 3-week plan
- Signal radar entries to watch (week1):
  * Access complete: binary (yes/no) — if "no" escalate to infra SRE within 24h.
  * First commit or doc: present/absent. Absence at day5 -> trigger follow-up.
  * Slack engagement: introduced + posted hello message. If no introduction by day2, manager ping.
  * Test pass locally: green/red. Red -> schedule troubleshooting pair.

FIRST 30 DAYS — success map and retention signals
- Outcomes (manager provides): 3 measurable outcomes with metrics (e.g., reduce tail latency config test by X%, implement feature flag for route Y, deliver 1 customer-facing template).
- Weekly checkpoints: 30min sync (manager), 30min mentor touch (peer), 60min product/feature context.
- Signals of strong onboarding (positive):
  * Ownership behavior: created a ticket + planned work for next sprint by week3.
  * Cross-team comms: participated in two cross-functional meetings.
  * Early win delivered: PR merged or doc published.
- Signals of risk (negative) — retention triggers that require escalation:
  * No measurable output by day14 (no PR/doc/ticket) -> people ops + manager call.
  * Persistent access gaps beyond 48h for core systems -> infra ops incident.
  * Low social signal (no 1:1 scheduled, no buddy touchpoint in week1) -> assign alternate buddy.
  * Confused role expectations (candidate asks >3 different clarifying questions about responsibilities) -> rewrite role one-pager and sync.

INTERVIEW DECISION RADAR (calibration guidance for panels)
- Purpose: convert qualitative debriefs into a concise decision radar (stoplight) to speed hiring decisions and reduce bias.
- Radar axes (use a 1–5 numeric scale):
  * Skill fit (role-specific technical skills)
  * Problem solving (signal: clarifies, explores tradeoffs, proposes measurable experiment)
  * Ownership & communication (writes tickets, communicates blockers)
  * Cultural ops-fit (collaboration, curiosity, async docs)
  * Risk factors (unknowns: visa, compensation misalignment, heavyweight restructure risk)
- Panel scoring: each interviewer records 1–2 bullet evidence lines + numeric score. Hiring manager aggregates median and writes decision rationale (70–200 words).
- Quick decision rules (recommended):
  * Accept if median >=4 on Skill + >=4 on Ownership.
  * Consider hire with plan if Skill 3–4 but Ownership >=4 (hiring manager must document ramp plan).
  * Pause/decline if Skill <=2 OR Risk factor flagged AND not mitigable.

SAMPLE INTERVIEW PROBES (fragments for eng roles) — drop-in questions:
- "Walk me through the last time you fixed a production perf regression. What was your measurement, hypothesis, and mitigation?"
- "How would you design a gradual rollout for a new inference model to 10% of traffic? What observability would you put in place?"
- "Show me a ticket you wrote (or explain the structure) — what made it effective?"
- Behavioral micro-probe: "Tell me about a time you changed direction late in a sprint. How did you communicate and what metrics did you track?"

MENTOR ROTATION & BUDDY PLAYBOOK
- Mentor selection criteria: someone on the team with 12+ months tenure and who has onboarded at least 2 hires.
- Rotation cadence: 30 days primary mentor -> optional swap at day30 if signals show mismatch. Always have a secondary buddy (peer) for context.
- Mentor responsibilities (first 30 days):
  * 2x 60m pairing sessions in week1, 1x 60m in week2, weekly 30m thereafter
  * Provide onboarding PR review within 48h for first 3 PRs
  * Invite new hire to two recurring team rituals (planning, critiques) within week2
- Mentor script (short):
  1) Day1: set expectations (what success looks like in 30 days).
  2) Week1: walkthrough common repo patterns and dev loop.
  3) Week2: review first ticket planning and demo feedback.
  4) Week4: retention check — what would make you stay?

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATES (copy/paste)
- Slack intro (manager): "Hi @here please welcome NAME, joining as ROLE on TEAM. Mentor: @mentor. Day1 intro lunch at 12pm PT. Quick context: they will focus on X for first 30d.
- Candidate offer check-in (people ops): short DM template to confirm start date + dietary restrictions + equipment preferences.

OPERATIONAL ESCALATION (fast path)
- Access failure: 24h -> infra oncall; 48h -> people ops escalation + equipment replacement priority.
- No output by day14: manager + people ops sync within 48h to create remediation plan; consider reduced scope + pair program.
- Distress signal (candidate expresses doubts): immediate 1:1 with manager same day and people ops follow-up within 48h.

DATA & METRICS (what to log in the communal tracker)
- Fields for tracker (one-line each): name, role, start_date, mentor, week1_output (Y/N), first_PR_date, 14d_status, 30d-outcome, retention_flag (none|watch|action).
- Suggested retention KPIs for people ops: % hires with first PR in 14 days, % hires with active buddy in week1, % hires with no access incidents.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (notes-to-self)
- Add a short 'first feedback' form for new hires sent at day7 (3 questions).
- Decide whether managers should own hardware ordering or people ops centralize (current mix is confusing).
- Hook into product onboarding templates (Confluence link above) to reduce duplicate docs.
- Experiment: "first-PR pairing" where mentor opens a stub PR before day1 to reduce intial friction. Pilot on infra team.

Appendix: quick debrief template for interviewers (copy into GitHub/PR):
- One-line summary: \"(hire / consider with plan / pass)\"
- Top 2 strengths (bullets)
- Top 2 risks (bullets)
- Suggested ramp plan (if any)
- Name of hiring manager + decision rationale (70–200 words)

End — keep this doc short, iterate frequently. If something felt manual more than once, convert it to a template and add to linked_artifacts.
